records.subject: Superionic Li6PS5Cl
records.object: Crossover from crystalline vibrations to relaxational ionic-diffusion dynamics
records.quote: Here we reveal a crossover from crystalline vibrations to relaxational dynamics of ionic diffusion in the superionic compound Li6PS5Cl, a candidate solid-state electrolyte.

records.subject: Superionic Li6PS5Cl
records.object: Vibrational density of states strongly deviating from quadratic Debye behavior
records.quote: Here we reveal a crossover from crystalline vibrations to relaxational dynamics of ionic diffusion in the superionic compound Li6PS5Cl, a candidate solid-state electrolyte.
context_quotes: By combining inelastic and quasi-elastic neutron-scattering measurements with first-principles-based machine-learned molecular dynamics simulations, we found that the vibrational density of states in the superionic state strongly deviates from the quadratic behaviour expected from the Debye law of lattice dynamics.
modality_evidence: By combining inelastic and quasi-elastic neutron-scattering measurements with first-principles-based machine-learned molecular dynamics simulations, we found that the vibrational density of states in the superionic state strongly deviates from the quadratic behaviour expected from the Debye law of lattice dynamics.

records.subject: Overdamped phonon quasiparticles
records.quote: Here we reveal a crossover from crystalline vibrations to relaxational dynamics of ionic diffusion in the superionic compound Li6PS5Cl, a candidate solid-state electrolyte.
context_quotes: The superionic dynamics emerges from overdamped phonon quasiparticles to give rise to a linear density of states characteristic of instantaneous normal modes in the liquid state.
records.conditions: Li6PS5Cl.

records.subject: PEDOT:PSS/p-MIM:TFSI transparent thin-film electrodes
records.quote: The PEDOT:PSS/p-MIM:TFSI thin-film electrodes are also biocompatible and conformally adhere to human skin; therefore, multimodal biosignals including electrocardiogram, electrooculogram, and electromyogram with high signal-to-noise ratios from exposed epidermis on human faces and arms under various measurement conditions mimicking daily activities are collected.
